newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: TENNIS-BECKER CRASHES OUT OF SWISS INDOORS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BECKER CRASHES OUT OF SWISS INDOORS.

text.p: Australian Open champion Boris Becker crashed out of the Swiss indoor championships on Thursday, failing to join U.S. and French Open winners Pete Sampras and Yevgeny Kafelnikov in the quarter- finals.

Becker, back in action for the first time since rupturing a tendon in his right-wrist at Wimbledon, appeared hampered by the injury, particularly while serving, as he fell 6-3 7-6 (7-4) to Jiri Novak of the Czech Republic.

Down 5-2 in the second set, Becker did mount a valiant comeback bid, fighting off five match points and forcing a tie- break before finally succumbing to the 21-year-old Czech, ranked 45th in the world.

"I was surprised by Novak, I thought he was only a clay court specialist," said Becker, seeded fourth and ranked sixth in the world. "But I'm happy with what I did here. At the beginning of the week I didn't have great hopes. I came back in the second set but I was always a step behind."

Sixth seed Stefan Edberg of Sweden, a three-time winner of the Swiss indoors, bowed out to lucky loser Marc Goellner of Germany 7-6 (9-7) 6-2, leaving Sampras and Kafelnikov as the tournament's only remaining seeds.

Playing in his first event since winning the U.S. Open, Sampras, the world number one, also appeared poised to make an early exit as he struggled past 18 year-old German wild card entry Tommy Haas 6-4 2-6 6-3.
Against Haas, Sampras looked only marginally sharper than he did in his first round match against another hard-hitting German, Alex Radulescu, who also forced him to three tough sets.

The American made a quick start against the German teenager, but Haas, rated by many to be the best German prospect since Becker, came back to dominate the second set. He broke Sampras to go 4-2 up but although he levelled the match, Sampras broke him three times in the third set to reach the last eight.
Sampras afterwards dismissed reports he was suffering from anaemia.
"It's all speculation," he said. "Whoever wrote that didn't know what they were talking about. It was just his opinion why I was getting tired on court.
"The fact is it's just conditioning. It's getting near the end of the year and it's not what it should be."
Kafelnikov, the third seed, had to work for his place in Friday's quarter-finals, fighting back to beat French qualifier Lionel Roux 4-6 6-3 6-4.
